---
title: Get started
description: Install smalldocs, make a site, preview it, and publish it.
order: 1
---

## Install

smalldocs needs Python 3.11 or later. Add it to a project as a tool for development:

```bash
uv add --dev smalldocs     # or: pip install smalldocs
```

If your site documents your package's API, install smalldocs in the same environment as the
package, so that it can import the package.

## Make a site

A site is a folder with a `_quarto.yml` file and some pages. A page is a `.qmd`, `.md` or `.ipynb`
file. This is the smallest site:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## _quarto.yml

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My project"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - about.qmd

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
```

## index.qmd

```markdown
---
title: My project
---

My project does one thing well. Read [about it](about.qmd).
```

## about.qmd

```markdown
---
title: About
---

## Who made it

We did.
```
:::

## Build it

```bash
smalldocs render            # the folder you are in
smalldocs render docs       # or another folder
```

smalldocs writes the site into `_site`, or into the folder that `project.output-dir` names. Each
build empties that folder first. Open `_site/index.html`, or serve the folder.

## Preview it

```bash
smalldocs preview docs
```

`preview` builds the site, serves it at `http://127.0.0.1:4200`, and opens your browser. When you
save a file, it builds the site again and the browser reloads. Give `--port` for another port.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Generated pages do not loop

A `pre-render` script, or the API reference, writes pages during a build. `preview` notes the files
after each build, so those writes do not start another build.
:::

## Publish it

To put the site on GitHub Pages:

```bash
smalldocs publish gh-pages docs
```

This builds the site, commits it to the `gh-pages` branch in a temporary worktree, and pushes the
branch to `origin`. It does not change your working tree or your current branch. In the settings of
the repository on GitHub, set Pages to deploy from the `gh-pages` branch.

You can also build the site in a GitHub Action and upload `_site`; smalldocs is one `pip install`.
